title: H. Longest Good Subsequence
statement:
Call an array b of size m good if the following conditions hold:

For example, the array [1,1,3,3,5] is good (where the permutation p=[2,1,5,3,4] satisfies the second requirement), but the array [1,1,2] isn't.

Note the empty array is considered to be good.

You are given an array a of size n. Find the length of the longest good subsequence^{†} of a.

^{∗}A permutation of length m is an array consisting of m distinct integers from 1 to m in arbitrary order. For example, [2,3,1,5,4] is a permutation, but [1,2,2] is not a permutation (2 appears twice in the array), and [1,3,4] is also not a permutation (m=3 but there is 4 in the array).

^{†}A sequence c is a subsequence of a sequence d if c can be obtained from d by the deletion of several (possibly, zero or all) element from arbitrary positions.

Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases t (1 ≤ t ≤ 10^4). The description of the test cases follows.

The first line of each test case contains an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 15,000) – the length of a.

The second line of each test case contains n integers a_1,a_2,…,a_n (1 ≤ a_i ≤ n) — denoting the array a.

It is guaranteed that the sum of n^2 does not exceed 15,000^2 over all test cases.

For each test case, output the length of the longest good subsequence of a on a new line.

In the first test case, the entire sequence is good.

In the second test case, the longest good subsequence is [1,2].

Input:
```
551 1 3 3 531 1 242 2 2 271 2 4 2 4 6 211
```

Output:
```
5
2
0
5
1
```
